newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - July 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The prime minister has removed Chatumongol Sonakul as permanent secretary for finance in what is seen as an attempt to launch his own economic salvage effort. The transfer comes as Rerngchai Marakanond bows to what he calls political pressure and resigns as governor of the Bank of Thailand. Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi, the deputy governor, is appointed to replace him. (BANGKOK POST, THE NATION)

- The government may stick with a half-baked economic and financial reform programme, jointly designed by the International Monetary Fund, for fear of losing control over its management of the economy. Both the ruling New Aspiration Party and the Chart Pattana Party have agreed not to plunge the country headlong into the full economic stabilisation course which would be prescribed by the IMF in return for stand-by credit. (THE NATION)

- ASEAN foreign ministers have received a letter from their Cambodian counterpart Ung Huot, on behalf of Second Premier Hun Sen, welcoming their help to restore political stability in Cambodia. The three members of an ASEAN mediation mission receive similar letters inviting them to travel to Phnom Penh. (THE NATION)

- Bangkok Bank will refuse new loans to the Alphatec Group if it fails to come up with clear financial and operational plans, the bank's Executive Chairman Chatri Sophonpanich says. He is responding to a statement made by Nakornthon Bank President Thamnu Wanglee that he would ask other creditor banks of the Alphatec Group to inject fresh loans amounting to 200-300 million baht to keep the group's activities going. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai Summit Autoparts Group will today sign an agreement with PT Timor Industri Komponen to form a joint venture to produce automotive parts for ASEAN automakers, including Indonesia's Timor national car project. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will witness the signing of the US$80 million contract for a project to manufacture automotive parts, components and accessories to supply the ASEAN market. (THE NATION)
